words.prose: {{ar:بَلْ}} ({{tr:bal}}) makes the ayah begin with correction before it names the corrected state. It reaches back to the previous claim in 68:26 and redirects the speakers into {{ar:نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ}} ({{tr:naḥnu maḥrūmūna}}): not a neutral continuation, but a replacement diagnosis. The replacement is sharper, moving from being in the wrong condition to being cut off from benefit. The particle does this at discourse scope rather than by governing the following words, so the next phrase remains its own nominative nominal sentence. Its short stopped shape gives the reclassification an abrupt pivot: a clipped correction, then the fuller self-label that lands the ayah.

topics.reason: QAC and translation support mark the particle as retractional or corrective; the local wording supports displacement of the prior predicate, while the prose avoids overclaiming a total logical cancellation beyond the local correction.

topics.reason: The particle is uninflected and non-governing, and the attachment evidence identifies the following words as a corrective nominal sentence.

words.prose: {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}) puts the speakers themselves in a separate subject slot before the predicate arrives. The pronoun is resolved by the preceding speech chain, so it means the garden owners already speaking in 68:26, not an inclusive audience or a generic class of deprived people. Its explicitness matters: the ayah could have leaned on context, but instead makes the group say 'we' before accepting the passive label. The pronoun gives first-person plurality without gender; then {{ar:مَحْرُومُونَ}} ({{tr:maḥrūmūna}}) supplies the masculine plural predicate agreement. The nasal sounds across the phrase bind the collective self to the deprivation label.

topics.reason: The cross-reference evidence resolves the pronoun to the prior plural speakers, while QAC identifies it as an independent first-person plural pronoun.

topics.reason: The nominal clause consists of an explicit plural subject and a passive participial predicate, supporting a stative group self-identification.

words.prose: {{ar:مَحْرُومُونَ}} ({{tr:maḥrūmūna}}) is the ayah's landing word: a masculine plural nominative predicate matching {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}), so the whole speaking group receives the same status. As a Form I passive participle, it makes them patients of deprivation while leaving the depriving agent unnamed; the grammar does not need to decide inside the word who caused the loss. As a bare predicate in a verbless nominal sentence, it assigns deprivation as a qualitative standing condition rather than narrating a completed deprivation event or naming a fixed class. It also leaves the object unstated, but the garden context supplies the expected harvest or provision, so the compact predicate means being cut off from what they had counted on. The root field of {{ar:ح ر م}} ({{tr:ḥ-r-m}}) lets deprivation feel boundary-like: the selected sense is access-denial, while sanctuary, consecration, and causative prohibition branches stay outside the local parse except as qualified background pressure. Against the garden-loss wording in 56:67, this word frames garden ruin as barred provision rather than debt-like liability. Against the prior diagnosis in 68:26, the matching participial cadence turns active lostness into passive affectedness. The nasal frame of the local phrase also binds the collective self to the final deprivation label. The same garden narrative that begins at 68:17 makes the reversal sharper: the would-be excluders now name themselves by deprivation. Echoes of the deprived-recipient label in 51:19 and 70:25 add another pressure, because a term associated with those lacking provision is now spoken by the garden owners about themselves.

topics.reason: QAC parses the word as masculine plural nominative and attachment evidence makes it the predicate of the explicit plural pronoun.

topics.headline: patients without named agent

topics.reason: The passive participle supports affected patienthood and agent suppression; because the attachment bundle gives no licensed implicit-agent row, the prose keeps the agent gap without listing candidates.

topics.headline: harvest access is left recoverable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader supplies the expected garden produce as the missing object, so the predicate is more specific than generic misfortune.
topics.reason: The predicate has no overt complement, and the accepted deprivation branch includes loss of hoped-for provision; the garden scene supplies the recoverable object.

topics.headline: deprivation is a standing condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees deprivation presented as the speakers' current identity rather than as a narrated event with a finite verb.
topics.reason: The word is a passive participial predicate in a nominal clause, not a finite passive verb.

topics.headline: condition, not named class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speakers assigned a qualitative condition in a direct subject-predicate frame.
topics.reason: The predicate is bare and separate from the subject, and Arabic nominal predication links the two without an overt copula.

topics.headline: deprivation feels like exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the loss as being placed outside access to a benefit, not merely as unlucky lack.
topics.reason: V4 supports deprivation and protected-boundary branches in the root field, but the local passive participle selects deprivation or access-denial; sanctuary and protected-precinct imagery is therefore kept as qualified boundary pressure, not as the local sense.

topics.headline: passive lane, not consecration entry

topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form I passive participle, while V4 lists consecration and causative prohibition elsewhere in the root field; the local form does not activate those branches as the selected meaning.

topics.headline: loss framed as exclusion, not liability

topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete contrast with 56:67, and the local root branch supports deprivation or exclusion rather than liability.

topics.headline: active lostness becomes passive deprivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the correction from 68:26 as a shift in agency: from the speakers' lostness to their being acted upon.
topics.reason: The preceding diagnosis is displaced by the corrective particle, and the local predicate is passive rather than active.

topics.headline: the ayah lands in one self-label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the whole scene contract into a final predicate that combines loss, exclusion, patienthood, and corrected self-definition.
topics.reason: The word closes the ayah, serves as the nominal predicate, and gathers the root-field boundary pressure with passive patient morphology and the preceding correction.

topics.headline: would-be excluders self-name as deprived

topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows connect the self-label to the same garden narrative begun at 68:17 and to the owners' exclusionary role within that narrative.

topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete parallels in 51:19 and 70:25; the contextual profile shows this passive-participle root-form group is not restricted to one referent class.

topics.reason: The local phrase repeats nasal sounds, and the final long plural ending pairs acoustically with the preceding ayah's participial ending while the meaning shifts.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive plural predicate mahrumun, sharpened by bal, names the speakers rather than merely describing a missing object.
baseline_models.mechanism: A hoped-for good is blocked or missed, and the collective nominal sentence converts that event into a shared condition of frustrated expectation.

activation_trace.role: Deprivation and failure to obtain the sought provision supplies both the lost good and the speakers' resulting state.

changed_reading.after: The speakers diagnose themselves collectively as people shut out from what they had already treated as obtainable.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Mahrumun is a passive state from the focus root, so it can foreground a barrier between persons and good rather than destruction of the good itself.
baseline_models.mechanism: Barring is relational: an object may remain conceptually available while access to it is closed. The utterance can therefore name exclusion, not only scarcity.

activation_trace.role: Forbidding and barring turns the predicate into an access relation with the speakers on its blocked side.

changed_reading.before: Their good has ceased to exist.
changed_reading.after: They have been placed on the prohibited side of a relation to the good they seek.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same focus root carries protected bounds and inviolable claims, allowing mahrumun to touch standing and entitlement as well as supply.
baseline_models.mechanism: Deprivation can be represented spatially as being outside a protected domain and legally as lacking a claim that secures access within it.

activation_trace.role: Protected bounds provide the spatial model in which the speakers find themselves outside an expected precinct.
The inviolable-claim branch shifts the loss from inventory alone to the standing that would make access secure.

changed_reading.after: The statement can also register loss of protected access or of the claim by which the speakers assumed the good was theirs.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening's uncut reward and the garden episode's repeated cutting language establish a continuity axis. Mahrumun then names the party whose expected flow has been severed.

activation_trace.role: Missing the hoped-for provision anchors the severed-flow reading in the focus predicate.
Cutting and diminution until extension ends supplies the negative image behind an explicitly unending reward.
Cutting and separation materializes the end of continuity in the garden itself.

structural_cues: An unsevered reward appears near the surah opening, while cutting recurs through the garden episode.
The focus sentence predicates deprivation of the people, not merely damage of the crop.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies uncut reward, repeated cutting, and deprivation; I infer a contrastive continuity axis joining them. A live alternative is that the cutting vocabulary is local to harvest and carries no wider contrast.

changed_reading.before: The owners have no crop on this occasion.
changed_reading.after: They occupy the cut-off side of a contrast between provision that continues and expectation whose extension has been severed.

context_deltas.mechanism: Active withholding is reversed into passive deprivation: the plan to bar a needy entrant becomes the owners' own position relative to the garden's good.

activation_trace.role: Deprivation of hoped-for good supplies the passive endpoint of the owners' prior excluding action.
Withholding the hand from giving establishes the active social role that the garden owners later enact.
Entry into an interior makes the planned exclusion concrete as denial of access.
Withholding and contraction characterize the owners' purposeful approach immediately before the reversal.

structural_cues: The earlier withholder-of-good description precedes the garden episode.
The owners whisper that no poor person shall enter, then call themselves deprived three verses later.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies withholding, a barred entrance, and the passive deprivation predicate; I infer a role-reversal arrow from denying access to suffering denied access. The alternative is non-retributive crop loss followed by an unrelated lament.

changed_reading.before: They are victims of an external loss.
changed_reading.after: They recognize themselves as occupying the very deprived position they intended to impose on another.

context_deltas.mechanism: The garden event functions as disclosure: a test acts while the owners are unseeing, and sight converts a hidden disposition into their explicit collective diagnosis.

activation_trace.role: The deprivation branch gives the disclosed condition its concrete object of frustrated provision.
Testing that makes a condition appear frames the episode as revelation rather than bare accident.
Hiddenness and heedlessness supply the pre-revelation state in which the owners remain unaware.
Visual seeing marks the transition from concealed condition to articulated recognition.

structural_cues: The episode is introduced as a test, the transformation occurs during sleep, and the declaration follows sight.
The plural nominal predicate describes what the speakers now understand themselves to be.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies testing, unawareness, sight, and self-predication; I infer that the event reveals a condition as well as causing loss. The alternative is that mahrumun names only the newly observed outcome.

changed_reading.before: The event newly makes them poor in produce.
changed_reading.after: The event also exposes to them a shared condition that their confident plan had kept hidden.

context_deltas.mechanism: Their refusal to introduce an exception into the plan is mirrored by an exceptionless outcome: none of the planners stands outside the collective mahrumun.

activation_trace.role: Barring supplies the total exclusion into which the whole first-person plural is gathered.
Making an exception by removing one item from a total supplies the missing operator whose absence leaves no owner exempt.

structural_cues: Failure to except follows the oath and precedes the complete overnight loss.
Nahnu and the masculine plural predicate include the planning group without an expressed exception.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an omitted exception and an all-group deprivation; I infer a formal reversal from no exception in planning to no exception from the result. The live alternative is the narrower conventional force of failing to qualify the oath.

changed_reading.before: The verse says only that the crop was withheld.
changed_reading.after: The collective wording also answers their exceptionless plan with an exceptionless exclusion of the planners themselves.

context_deltas.mechanism: The owners imagine the garden as an interior whose gate they control. The focus reverses that geometry: the intended gatekeepers discover themselves outside the protected access they presumed.

activation_trace.role: Protected bounds turn deprivation into a spatial relation between an interior good and those now outside it.
Literal entry into an interior supplies the gate whose control the owners claim.
The abasement of poverty identifies the socially vulnerable person assigned to remain outside.
Contraction and withholding make the imagined garden boundary deliberately restrictive.

structural_cues: The no-entry statement immediately precedes the approach, sight, and focus declaration.
The sentence shifts attention from the garden as object to the owners' location in an access relation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an interior, an excluded poor person, restrictive intent, and protected-boundary imagery; I infer a gate reversal placing the gatekeepers outside. The alternative remains straightforward destruction with no surviving spatial model.

changed_reading.before: The owners no longer possess usable produce.
changed_reading.after: The would-be gatekeepers experience deprivation as finding themselves outside the garden-access relation they meant to police.

context_deltas.mechanism: The movement from purposeful resolve and claimed capability to mahrumun collapses agency. The capacity root's own constriction branch makes the reversal especially sharp: presumed power narrows into no usable share.

activation_trace.role: Failure to obtain the sought good supplies the endpoint at which asserted agency proves ineffective.
Purposeful aim supplies the directed intention with which the owners begin their approach.
Effective capability supplies the owners' self-position immediately before the failed encounter.
Constriction to a slight measure activates the latent opposite hidden within the same capacity cue.

structural_cues: Qadirin stands two verses before mahrumun, with visual disorientation between them.
The first-person plural moves from a capability posture to a passive deprivation predicate.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies intention, capability, a constriction branch, and deprivation; I infer an agency-to-constriction reversal. The alternative is that the constriction branch is inactive and qadirin means only confidence in carrying out the plan.

changed_reading.before: Their material stock disappears while their agency remains conceptually intact.
changed_reading.after: Their declaration confesses the collapse of presumed capacity into a condition where no intended power can secure a share.

context_deltas.mechanism: Sight first produces a spatial diagnosis, 'we are astray,' but bal replaces it with a relational diagnosis, 'we are deprived.' The place is not merely unrecognized; their status toward its good has changed.

activation_trace.role: Missing the sought provision supplies the corrected diagnosis introduced by bal.
Visual perception initiates the interpretive sequence rather than settling it.
Straying from a path supplies the first, spatial explanation that the focus sentence overturns.
Losing an object keeps a second sense of loss alive even as bal sharpens its cause and relation.

structural_cues: The focus ayah directly follows the visual encounter and the statement 'we are astray.'
Bal marks correction or escalation between two first-person plural diagnoses.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sight, straying or loss, and bal followed by deprivation; I infer a correction from wrong-location explanation to changed-status explanation. The alternative is simple rhetorical intensification between near-synonymous expressions of loss.

changed_reading.before: They think they have reached the wrong place or lost their way.
changed_reading.after: They correct perception into diagnosis: the place is theirs to recognize, but they no longer stand in an obtaining relation to its yield.

context_deltas.mechanism: Subsequent confession and judgment language reactivate the focus root's claim dimension. 'We are deprived' can sound less like an accusation that their right was violated and more like a self-verdict after they withheld another's right.

activation_trace.role: Inviolable claim and pact-protection make entitlement and standing available inside the focus predicate.
Withholding or confinement from a right gives the owners' later confession a rights-based social content.
Judgment between parties supplies the juridical frame in which their declaration can function as a verdict.

structural_cues: The owners move from deprivation to confession of wrongdoing.
The later discourse repeatedly challenges unsupported judgments and claims.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an inviolable-claim branch, confession of right-withholding, and judgment language; I infer that the lament is also a self-verdict about standing. The alternative is that the legal register belongs only to the later audience and does not feed back into the garden speech.

changed_reading.before: They complain as entitled owners whose due property was denied.
changed_reading.after: They begin to concede that their presumed claim cannot be asserted unchanged after a plan built on denying another's access.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later hope for substitution prevents the nominal predicate from hardening into a permanent identity. Deprivation becomes an interval in which desire can turn from the lost object toward a different giver and possible replacement.

activation_trace.role: Constrained provision and missed expectation supply the real present condition whose finality is being tested.
One thing standing in place of another opens the deprived state toward replacement rather than permanence.
Desire turning toward or away from an object supplies the reorientation that follows the loss.

structural_cues: The same speakers soon voice hope for a better substitute.
Their grammatical state remains present and collective, but the narrative does not leave desire fixed on the destroyed garden.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies present deprivation, possible substitution, and redirected desire; I infer that the predicate names an interval rather than an irreversible essence. The alternative is that their hope is wishful and does not actually weaken the finality of the focus diagnosis.

changed_reading.before: Mahrumun fixes the speakers in a terminal identity of deprivation.
changed_reading.after: It names a truthful present state that may become the hinge from possessive certainty to redirected desire and replacement.

surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus root explicitly includes defeat at gambling as preventing an opponent from obtaining what was hoped for.

activation_trace.role: Gambling defeat as deprivation recasts the owners as players who lose the very gain they counted as secured.
A trimmed stick cast for lots supplies an allotment mechanism beyond the pen's ordinary image.
Dividing and assigning a share makes their oath also resonate with the distribution they tried to prevent.

changed_reading.before: The owners are passive sufferers of an unforeseeable shortage.
changed_reading.after: As an allotment analogy, they are failed monopolizers whose confident wager for every share leaves them with none.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because mahrumun is not the ordinary term for ritual consecration; it remains worth carrying because protected precinct and consecration are focus-root branches activated by circling and later worship language. Render it as an 'as though the garden became untouchable' spatial echo, not a claim that the owners literally entered ritual status.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Protected precinct and ritual restriction are both available branches of the sole rooted focus word.

activation_trace.role: An inviolable precinct supplies the bounded garden-space from which ordinary taking is suspended.
Ritual consecration supplies a temporary regime in which previously normal acts become restricted.
Circling around a thing gives the overnight visitation a precinct-like spatial motion.
Worship through glorification keeps the ritual register live immediately after the focus declaration.

changed_reading.before: The garden is merely ruined and therefore valueless.
changed_reading.after: In a contained spatial echo, the visitation makes the garden as inaccessible as a restricted precinct and its owners unable to perform their intended taking.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates document and title imagery far after the garden scene; it remains anchored through the focus branch of inviolable claim and the packet's written-decree and right-document branches. Downstream prose should call it a legal-document analogy that questions entitlement, not evidence of a literal deed or contract.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus root's claim and pact branch permits deprivation to include loss of secure title or standing.

activation_trace.role: Inviolable claim and right provide the entitlement whose security the owners had presumed.
A written fixing that imposes judgment supplies the imagined documentary guarantee challenged by the later questions.
A record functioning as a document of right supplies the title-deed analogy for a claim that must actually be warranted.

changed_reading.before: Ownership itself guarantees the owners an indefeasible claim to the yield.
changed_reading.after: Their cry can be heard, analogically, as discovery that possession furnished no unconditional title securing the good against every claim and judgment.

strongest_changes: The planned withholders become the passively withheld, turning loss into a social role reversal.
Bal corrects visual or spatial disorientation into recognition of a changed relation to provision.
The move from qadirin to mahrumun collapses asserted capacity into constriction and failed agency.
Later substitution and redirected desire keep the diagnosis truthful without making it a permanent identity.
summary.what_was_special: The sole focus root sustained economic, social, spatial, and juridical readings at once. Context did not merely explain the lost garden: it activated reversals of giver and receiver, gatekeeper and excluded person, capacity and constriction, claim and self-verdict, while the lot, precinct, and title images remained live under explicit containment.
remaining_uncertainties: The retributive arrow from excluding the poor to being excluded is abductively strong but is still supplied by the reader rather than stated as a causal formula.
Protected-precinct, ritual, gambling, and documentary branches are visibly anchored but more form-distant than ordinary deprivation and should remain exploratory.
The later legal and replacement cues may reshape the focus retrospectively, or they may primarily address the surah's wider audience rather than the garden owners.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Correction from lost place to lost provision.** *Bal* explicitly revises 68:26, and `ح ر م B008` supplies deprivation of gift, good, or provision. The pronoun *naḥnu* relocates the defect from the garden's identity to their own condition. I infer corrected perception -> ownership of consequence; the ayah is the first precise recognition that they, not the route, are the locus of loss.
2. **The barrers become barred.** `ح ر م B001` supplies forbidding and barring, while their prior speech barred the poor from entry. The packet supplies both directions; I infer their exclusionary act does not mechanically cause the event, but the narrative arranges a reversal in which attempted barring is answered by deprivation. *Maḥrūmūn* thus carries the shape of their own policy back onto them.
3. **A violated claim to inviolability.** `ح ر م B003/B006` supplies protected bounds and inviolable claim. Their possessive language treated the garden as protected entitlement, but the event crosses that assumed boundary. I infer property was mistaken for absolute inviolability; the ayah strips that assumption while leaving ordinary possession distinguishable from guaranteed access.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:32 turns deprivation into desire for replacement, so recognition does not end in mere negation. 68:34's gardens of favor then show the larger correction: provision is not abolished but received within guarding and lordship rather than presumed inviolable ownership.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Deprivation as the return of a violated protected claim.** Fixed `مَحْرُومُونَ` activates `ح ر م B008` (missing sought provision) together with `ح ر م B006` (an inviolable claim, pact, or respect). The barred poor person in 68:24 and the owners' loss of the crop supply two opposed claimants; I infer that denying another's protected access rebounds as loss of their own access. Their correction therefore recognizes a relational deprivation, not simply missing property.
2. **A boundary that fails to protect its makers.** The same fixed root activates `ح ر م B003` (protected precinct and bounds). The owners attempt to police entry in 68:24, but 68:26 shows that the bounded place no longer answers to them; I infer that exclusion was treated as protection even though it could not secure the enclosed good. `مَحْرُومُونَ` reads as being placed outside the very protected relation they tried to monopolize.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 68:32 redirects desire toward the Lord and possible replacement. That later reorientation made fixed deprivation read as exclusion from a protected relation (`ح ر م B006/B003`), not merely from one crop.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Rain or milk stops, the final remnant is drawn, an animal or person waits for return, and deprivation names the failed flow.

concept_map.definition: Bir eylemin, nesnenin veya hakkın yapılmasına, kullanılmasına ya da çiğnenmesine izin verilmemesidir. Yıkılmış bir yerleşimin geri dönmesiyle ilgili sabit kalıpta ise anlam, olanaksızlık ile kesin bir geri dönmeme hükmü arasında yorumlanır.

facets.statement: Temel anlam, izin verilenin karşıtı olarak hükmen veya kural gereği yasaklanmış şeydir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir yandan genel cinsel dürtüyü, öte yandan koyun, keçi ve benzeri dişilerin erkeği istemesini anlatır; köpek örneği aktarılırken kullanımın yalnızca çift tırnaklılara özgü olduğu yönünde de bir sınırlama verilir. Bu nedenle genel dürtü ile dişi hayvanın çiftleşme isteği ayrılmalı, hayvan türlerinin kapsamı kesinleştirilmemelidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: İnsan veya erkek hayvandaki genel cinsel dürtü ile dişi hayvanın erkeği isteme durumu ayrıdır; tür kısıtı kaynakta tam kararlı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın kapsam, genel cinsel dürtüyü ve dişi hayvanın erkeği istemesini ayrı yönler olarak verir; tartışmalı tür sınırını genellemez.

concept_map.definition: Cinsel dürtünün yükselmesi veya dişi bir hayvanın çiftleşmek üzere erkeği istemesidir. Hayvan kullanımı özellikle koyun ve keçi gibi türlerde aktarılır, ancak kapsamın yalnızca bu türlerle sınırlı olup olmadığı açık değildir.

facets.statement: Kullanım, insanda veya hayvanda cinsel dürtünün ve çiftleşme isteğinin yükselmesini bildirir.
Dişi koyun, keçi ve benzeri hayvanların erkeği istemesi özel bir gerçekleşmedir.
Hayvan kullanımının yalnızca çift tırnaklılara özgü olduğu söylenirken köpek örneğinin de verilmesi kapsamı belirsiz bırakır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıtlar genel cinsel dürtü ile dişi hayvanın çiftleşme isteğini birlikte aktarır; koyun ve keçi örnekleri belirgindir, fakat köpek örneği ile çift tırnaklılara özgülük iddiası arasında kapsam gerilimi vardır.
